title: Incident Communication Playbook and Postmortem Framework
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview:
This page centralizes incident communication templates, a standardized postmortem framework, and a small library of runbook fragments to use during production incidents. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders, support leads, and product owners who will craft public-facing messages and internal timelines.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents that impact customer-facing API availability, latency SLOs, embedding generation failures, and scheduled major degradations.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance notifications (see maintenance-announce template in product-notifications).

Key contacts and roles:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns the incident timeline and public communications cadence.
- Communications Lead (Comms): owns message drafting and approvals for status page, email, and social updates.
- SRE Lead: technical lead for mitigation and escalation to infra or networking.
- Product/Customer Success Liaison: coordinates customer-specific messages and QBR follow-ups.

Severity taxonomy (quick reference):
1) Sev 0 (P0): Platform down for >5% of customers or system-level outage impacting normal use; requires page, engage IC within 5 minutes.
2) Sev 1 (P1): Major degradation (latency >2x SLO or errors >5% sustained 5m).
3) Sev 2 (P2): Partial feature loss / intermittent errors.
4) Sev 3 (P3): Low-impact or informational incidents.

Incident lifecycle (high-level):
1. Detection: alert triggers, first responder acknowledges (Slack / PagerDuty).
2. Triage: initial tags (sev, components), assemble responders, assign IC.
3. Containment & Mitigation: apply runbook steps, enable fallbacks, route traffic.
4. Communication: status page + customer comms per cadence.
5. Resolution & Recovery: verify tests and SLOs returned.
6. Postmortem: RCA, action items, timeline and distribution.

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1. Confirm the alert is valid: check metrics (latency, error rate, 5xx). CLI: 
   - curl -s https://metrics.redwood.internal/api?query=request_latency | jq .
2. Identify likely impacted services (eg: predictor-gpu-01, routing-proxy).
3. Capture reproducible steps / request IDs.
4. Assign Incident Commander and Communications lead.
5. Create incident channel: #incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}-{{short-title}} and pin this playbook.
6. If Sev0/P1, publish first status page message within 15 minutes.

Communication cadence (recommended):
- Initial: within 15 minutes for Sev0/P1, 30–60 minutes for P2 if customer-impacting.
- Updates: every 30 minutes for active mitigation; every 2 hours for extended events.
- Resolution: when all customer-impacting symptoms cleared + verification.
- Postmortem published: within 7 business days (draft), final within 14 days.

Status page templates (short):
- Title: "Investigating: Increased error rate for Redwood API"
- Body (short): "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting a subset of API requests. Engineers are triaging the issue. Impact: intermittent failures for some customers. Next update: in 30 minutes. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}."

Status page templates (detailed update):
- Title: "Mitigation in progress: routing fallback enabled"
- Body (detailed): "What happened: We observed a rising 5xx rate in predictor cluster 'predictor-gpu-01' beginning at 03:18 UTC.
What we are doing: Traffic was re-routed to 'predictor-gpu-02' and a temporary autoscale policy triggered.
Impact: Reduced but not eliminated errors for customers in us-east-1.
Next steps: Performing root cause analysis and monitoring for regression. Next update: 30 minutes. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}."

Customer email template (technical customers):
Subject: "Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Redwood API partial disruption (root cause in progress)"
Body: 
Hello {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

We are currently investigating an issue impacting a subset of API requests to Redwood. Symptoms include elevated HTTP 5xx errors and increased latency. We have enabled routing fallbacks and are continuing work to fully remediate.

Current status: Mitigation in progress.
Estimated ETA to recovery: TBD — next update by {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}.
How this may affect you: Some requests may fail or receive delayed responses; retries are recommended where idempotent.

If you have critical workflows at risk, please reply to this email or contact your Customer Success rep: {{CS_REP}}.

We will share a full postmortem when available.

Thanks,
Redwood Incident Response

Public tweet/status blurb (short):
"We are investigating an incident impacting Redwood API performance. Engineers are actively working on mitigation. Status page: <https://status.redwood.ai/incident/{{INCIDENT_ID}}>"

Escalation matrix (summary):
- First responder (on-call): 0–10 minutes.
- IC appointed if incident remains unresolved after 10 minutes.
- If IC cannot contain in 30 minutes escalate to SRE Lead.
- >60 minutes escalate to CTO and Customer Success Head for major-impact events.

Runbook fragment: high 5xx error rate on text-generation endpoint
1. Confirm spike: query 5xx by endpoint for last 5m.
   - metrics query example: curl -s "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api?query=sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\", route=~\"/v1/generate\"}[5m]))" | jq .
2. Check predictor node health: ssh predictor-gpu-01 sudo systemctl status redwood-predictor
3. If OOM on node: cordon node, scale up replacement pool: kubectl scale deployment/predictor --replicas=4 -n inference
4. Enable fallback version: set routing policy: redwoodctl routing set --route "generate" --variant "generate-v2-fallback"
5. Monitor error rate and latency; if not improving re-route all traffic gradually.

Postmortem framework (mandatory sections):
- Title, incident ID, severity, owner(s), timeline (minute-granular), impact summary (customers, SLOs), root cause, contributing factors, mitigation steps, corrective actions (with owners and due dates), follow-ups, lessons learned, and verification plan.

Postmortem template (example short):
Title: "P1 — Increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate — {{INCIDENT_ID}}"
Summary: One-line summary of what happened and primary impact.
Timeline: 1) 03:15 UTC alert fired (5xx spike); 2) 03:22 IC assigned; 3) 03:30 routing fallback applied; 4) 04:05 error rate returned to baseline.
Root cause: Memory leak in model-serving process triggered by rare tokenizer input pattern.
Contributing factors: Lack of aggressive heap-growth monitoring and a config drift in image version.
Corrective actions:
- Patch: fix tokenizer edge-case and release v1.2.3 (owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2025-01-30)
- Monitoring: add heap growth alert (owner: eng-sre, due: 2024-11-05)
Verification: run synthetic traffic with offending token patterns in staging for 72h.

Postmortem cadence and review:
- Draft PM distributed to the Engineering All channel within 7 business days.
- 30-minute review meeting scheduled within 10 business days with IC, SRE, product owner, and Customer Success.
- Action item tracking in JIRA with label: incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}.

On-call rotation administration (best practices):
- Primary on-call window: 09:00–21:00 local office hours; nights/weekends covered by second-tier rotations.
- Runbook owner must review rotation schedule quarterly and confirm backups before each major release.
- Use PagerDuty schedules with auto-handoff; verify escalation policies monthly via game days.
- For extended incidents, rotate responders every 4 hours to prevent burnout.

Game day exercise plan (quarterly):
- Objective: validate public communications, routing fallback, and postmortem process.
- Pre-reqs: staging environment mirroring routing config; test customer account; scripted fault injection.
- Steps: 1) Trigger staged 5xx spike; 2) On-call responds using this playbook; 3) Publish status page message; 4) Complete postmortem draft within 48 hours; 5) Retrospective with outcomes and JIRA actions.

Measurement and SLOs to include in incident write-ups:
- Error rate (5xx) threshold: 0.5% rolling 5m baseline; incident threshold: >5% sustained 5m.
- P99 latency for generate: baseline 1.2s; incident alarm if >2.4s.
- Customer impact: number of customers with failed requests (>1% of active customers is P1).

Retention, publishing and confidentiality guidance:
- All incident artifacts (timeline, slack logs) stored in incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/{{INCIDENT_ID}}/ (access: eng + cs leads).
- Draft postmortem default visibility: internal. If customer-impacting and public comms issued, produce a redacted public summary for the status page.
- Legal or security-sensitive incidents: set confidentiality to "restricted" and route draft to Legal and Security reviewers before wider distribution.

Appendix: Quick command cheatsheet
- Create incident channel: slack-cli create-channel --name incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}
- Pin runbook: slack-cli pin --channel incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}} --file incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026.json
- Publish status update via API: curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/incidents -d '{"id":"{{INCIDENT_ID}}","status":"investigating","message":"{{MESSAGE}}"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{STATUS_API_KEY}}'

Notes and references:
- Related runbooks: see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks and /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024
- For large-customer playbooks and legal templates, contact Legal and Customer Success to pre-approve wording.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Priya Menon (eng-sre liaison). Review quarterly or after any P1/P0 incident.
